figures.title: Adding 10 m wind speed misses the planned threshold for reducing solar forecast loss
subtitle: XGBoost tree models train on April 2024–June 2025; forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026.
Each XGBoost model uses 500 squared-error trees, maximum depth 6, and learning rate 0.05. Each tree samples 80% of rows and can use all columns.
These training and scoring dates define Fold A. All scored forecast times are included.
The comparison adds wind speed 10 m above ground to lean solar’s 13 real inputs; all other retained inputs stay the same.
Both input sets use corrected weather processing; duplicate retained inputs keep all XGBoost models at 24 training columns.
Squared-error models fit each meter separately. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble.
Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is better.
The fair-CRPS correction assumes independent draws; its use with weather-ensemble values is diagnostic.
The plotted comparison uses matched forecasts and observations and weights solar meters and three random-seed fits equally.
A seed sets the random choices in a training run.
Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or transfer to new meters.
The mean loss reduction is 0.025 capacity points, below the planned 0.15-point threshold; the solar ladder stops at this first addition.
The stopping rule uses the mean across equally weighted meters and three fits. Later solar additions are not run, and lean solar is not adopted under this plan.
The primary 95% month-and-seed interval for the loss difference is -0.063 to 0.022 points; benefit remains unresolved under that method.
The equal-month difference is -0.021 points, with a t-interval of -0.037 to -0.005. Loss is lower in 9 of 12 months.
The equal-month estimate weights months equally and averages the three fits first, treating fitting-seed variation differently from the primary interval.
The stopping decision is separate from statistical evidence of benefit.
Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Frozen capacity is used only for scoring.
